claim: LLM competitive-programming evaluation in the literature is conducted as whole-submission pass@1 against a handful of public test cases, with no per-test-case/partial-credit granularity reported.
stance_target: No existing work applies per-requirement/partial-credit evaluation protocols to competitive programming code
scope_conditions: 315 Codeforces problems via CodeContests dataset, GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 4.6, pass@1 against max 3 public test cases
quoted_support: Each solution is executed against a maximum of three public test cases... If a solution fails multiple test cases, the worst verdict is recorded based on the following priority list: Compile Error, Runtime Error, Time Limit Exceeded, Wrong Answer, Accepted.

claim: Wrong Answer is the overwhelmingly dominant failure verdict for both GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 4.6 on competitive programming, not compile or runtime errors.
stance_target: Nature of LLM failures on algorithmic/competitive code
scope_conditions: 315 balanced Codeforces problems, CoT prompting condition
quoted_support: Wrong Answer (WA) accounts for 92.0% (183/199) of GPT-4o's failures and 69.6% (80/115) of Claude's failures.

claim: Forcing zero-shot Chain-of-Thought prompting degrades GPT-4o's competitive-programming accuracy (46.0% to 36.8% AC rate), reversing the usual CoT benefit seen on NLP reasoning benchmarks.
stance_target: CoT prompting effectiveness for algorithmic code generation
quoted_support: forcing CoT aggressively penalizes GPT-4o, dropping its pass rate from 46.0% to 36.8% and exacerbating a critical weakness in Greedy logic.
numbers: Greedy category: 28.9% CoT pass rate for GPT-4o

claim: Both frontier models collapse to near-zero pass rates on Hard-tier dynamic programming and binary search problems regardless of prompting strategy.
stance_target: Algorithmic difficulty ceiling for LLM code generation
quoted_support: GPT-4o's collapse at the Hard tier is most severe in DP and Binary Search, where it fails every problem (0%).
